runners_data.name: Benbecula
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with only one start (fifth over 6f on good), so form is thin, but Kevin Stott's positive book and Kevin Ryan's sharp juveniles on good ground make this worth monitoring; style is unclassified, and its best hope is to slot into a handy position and see out the straight strongly.

runners_data.name: Blue Pete
runners_data.note: Placed third over 6f at Southwell on its latest run but is a genuine hold-up horse shifted into midfield on the map simply because the rear of the field is over-subscribed; P J McDonald will attempt to find a rhythm, but 40 days off and a modest form line including a seventh on good ground tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Deputy Vice
runners_data.note: The most exposed runner in the field with four starts all showing competitive finishing positions (3-4-4-3), running well without winning on both good and soft ground at 6f; naturally a horse that comes from the back, but with so many rivals operating similarly, Kaiya Fraser faces a navigation challenge in finding clean air late.

runners_data.name: Eagles Eternal
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed debut runner for Jim Goldie, whose yard has been in fair 14-day form (4/30); going preference and style are unknown, creating genuine uncertainty, but freshness and a capable handler mean it cannot be ignored if it jumps cleanly and finds a prominent berth early.

runners_data.name: Pulse Of Fire
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, stepping up from a seventh-place debut over 5f on good ground, but the key factor here is that no rival is likely to seriously challenge for the lead; Ed Walker's juveniles often show improvement second time out, and Ashley Lewis (3lb claim) retains the ride, though STYLE_FIT flags that a stronger pace could expose limitations.

runners_data.name: Sankhum Galaxy
runners_data.note: Two runs both resulting in double-figure finishes on good ground at 6f raise serious doubts about its competitiveness at this level, and a fade pattern is also flagged; Aiden Brookes has limited room for positional improvement from the back of a packed field.

runners_data.name: Through The Gate
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Harry Eustace, whose yard has been quiet on the 14-day figures (0/17); going and style are entirely unknown, making assessment speculative, but Hector Crouch is a capable pilot and Eustace is respected with well-prepared first-time-out juveniles.

runners_data.name: Kirton Angel
runners_data.note: Posted a solid third on its only start over 6f on good ground and Cam Hardie knows the horse well after 61 days off; Richard and Peter Fahey have strong 14-day strike rates (8/61) and this is a natural prominent-type that could easily slot in second or third behind Pulse Of Fire and produce a telling late challenge.

runners_data.name: Sweet Distraction
runners_data.note: Only run came over an extended 8f on soft ground, both the trip and conditions very different from today's 6f on good; Oliver Stammers faces a stiff ask dragging form across two very different race shapes, and the fade-in-finish flag compounds the concern significantly.

races.paceDynamic: Pulse Of Fire is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no natural rival for the lead, should secure a comfortable, uncontested position from the outset over Redcar's straight six furlongs on good ground. That lone-leader scenario creates a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than a furious early burn, which historically favours horses able to sit close to the pace and pounce from a handy position in the final two furlongs. The cluster of genuine hold-up types — Blue Pete, Deputy Vice, Sankhum Galaxy, Kirton Angel, and Sweet Distraction — means the rear half of the field will be congested, and several will fail to find the clear daylight they need in a race that will not truly stretch out until late. This shape decisively favours prominent, patient horses who can track Pulse Of Fire within two lengths and unleash a sustained finish, rather than deep closers who need a strong pace to reel in. The field contains more hold-up types than can practically operate from the back, with Blue Pete and Deputy Vice — both true hold-up horses — redistributed to midfield on the map; in practice, Pulse Of Fire and any early-stepping debutants (Eagles Eternal, Through The Gate) are most likely to actually secure the front positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pulse Of Fire Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Pulse Of Fire leads unchallenged and the pace is moderate, allowing prominent trackers to time their challenge from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Pulse Of Fire sets a steady, controlled tempo and any horse able to sit within a length or two in second or third position is handed a perfect stalking platform; the absence of a pace rival means the lead is never truly pressured and energy is conserved for the final furlong sprint.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debutant Disrupts Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Eagles Eternal or Through The Gate breaks smartly and pushes Pulse Of Fire into a faster-than-expected early gallop.
scenarios.body: A genuinely contested pace increases the tempo and brings hold-up horses more into play by the time the field straightens for home; runners who can settle just off a genuine pace in third or fourth will be best placed if the early leaders tire in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and the prominent horses tie up, allowing the hold-up runners to cut through late.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability shape because most true closers in this field have been redistributed from their natural rear position and are unlikely to find the clear passage they need in a steadily-run race over six furlongs; only a genuine collapse of the leaders would make this viable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Open Tactical Mess
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners break erratically or jockeys jostle for position in the early stages, scrambling the anticipated order.
scenarios.body: A chaotic early phase would compress the field and negate Pulse Of Fire's anticipated advantage, producing a messy sprint finish where positional luck plays a greater role than pure form; unexposed or lightly raced runners with unknown tactical profiles could benefit disproportionately.

watchPoints.text: Kirton Angel — the Fahey yard is firing (8/61 over 14 days) and its sole start was a promising third over today's exact course and distance on good ground; if Cam Hardie slots it directly behind Pulse Of Fire, it is perfectly placed for the dominant scenario.

Pulse Of Fire — if Ashley Lewis allows the pace to drop too low, prominent rivals will have an effortless lead to track and the scenario collapses into a blanket sprint finish where Pulse Of Fire's stamina at 6f (only run was 5f) may be tested; watch the early gallop fractions.

Blue Pete and Deputy Vice — both genuine hold-up horses, both unable to get their natural position with the rear of the field congested; if P J McDonald or Kaiya Fraser gets caught in traffic through the final two furlongs, their true finishing ability will never be seen.

Eagles Eternal and Through The Gate — two complete unknowns making their debuts; either could break sharply and push Pulse Of Fire into a contested pace, fundamentally altering the race shape from controlled to genuinely run, so watch the stalls break carefully.

Sweet Distraction — its only run was over 8f on soft ground and today is 6f on good, a significant switch in both trip and conditions; if it shows any early foot it would be a surprise, but monitor in case the drop in trip paradoxically produces an unexpected prominent showing.

runners_data.name: Finn Ironside
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up horse in fair recent form (won last time, 4 days ago) for Ivan Furtado, but the very short turnaround and a genuine run-style mismatch in a slowly-run race temper optimism — his natural closer's game is compromised when the pace doesn't fire.
runners_data.comment: Finn Ironside arrives on the back of a win last time out and a second two starts back, bringing sharp recent form that makes him the pick despite a quick four-day turnaround; he has run over today's distance and going before, and carries 141 lb from stall 12.

runners_data.name: Emery Down
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave takes the ride on this consistent John Ryan-trained four-year-old who has placed on good ground at seven furlongs and races prominently — the pace map suits him well, and his recent form line of 261 shows he is knocking at the door.
runners_data.comment: Emery Down showed she can win when landing a success most recently, but four finishes outside the places in her last six starts suggest inconsistency; she has run over today's trip and going, carries 140 lb from stall one, and an official mark of 65 keeps her competitive.

runners_data.name: The Childe Of Hale
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's hold-up type has finished in double figures across recent good-ground runs and the form figures on this surface (0, 9, 10) make it very hard to make a case; 25 days off and no win or place on comparable going further dims the outlook.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and drawn in stall 18, The Childe Of Hale faces an uphill task, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns after 25 days off; a trainer striking at just 4% recently does him no favours.

runners_data.name: Luminous Warrior
runners_data.note: In-form hold-up horse for Christopher Kellett who has won twice and placed twice in five recent good-ground starts — his record genuinely suits the surface, but Jason Hart will need something to go wrong for the pace-setters for this natural closer to deliver at 7f.
runners_data.comment: Luminous Warrior has back-to-back wins and a second last time out to recommend him, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but a weight of 139 lb, an official mark of 64, and our rating ranking him 15th of 18 make him hard to fancy at face value.

runners_data.name: Camera Shy
runners_data.note: Michael Dods runner who naturally wants to come from off the pace, but with so many hold-up types in this field his race position will be further up than he'd like — the style compromise in a slowly-run race is real, and his recent form figures on good turf (4, 7) don't encourage.
runners_data.comment: Camera Shy showed he can win, a winner six starts back, but has been beaten into fifth or lower in his last three outings; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 137 lb from stall eight, and the quick seven-day turnaround is a potential concern.

runners_data.name: Mayo County
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's five-year-old has genuine good-ground form at seven furlongs including two wins and four places in eight comparable starts, but 82 days off the track is a notable query and his natural hold-up style is squeezed by a field already crowded at the rear.
runners_data.comment: Returning after 82 days off and ranked 14th of 18 on our figures, Mayo County faces a stiff ask, and an unplaced effort last time out does little to inspire confidence, though she does bring distance and going experience and a win in her last six starts to the table.

runners_data.name: Uncertainty
runners_data.note: Simon Whitaker's three-year-old has not placed on good ground yet from six attempts and has been running at six furlongs; the step to seven furlongs, 40 days off, and an out-of-role map position combine to make this a difficult race to win.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Uncertainty is yet to show the consistency her experience over today's trip and going suggests she is capable of, though a 40-day freshener and a rating of 64 offer slim encouragement from stall seven at 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Cavallo Pazzo
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for Daragh Bourke returning after a striking 335-day absence — the layoff alone is a significant concern, and his best recent efforts have come on softer ground or over distances longer than today's seven furlongs.
runners_data.comment: Cavallo Pazzo holds a rating of 69 against an official mark of 57, suggesting he is well treated on paper and represents a live threat from stall 17, having experience of today's trip and going; the concern is a 335-day absence leaves his current fitness an open question.

runners_data.name: Sun Of Dolly
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type for John Gallagher with a placed run at seven furlongs on good ground (2nd) in recent history — the Conor Whiteley claim is useful for the weight, but apprentice-led closers in a 18-runner slowly-run race face a tough task.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 16 of 18 on our figures, Sun Of Dolly is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's distance and going before and comes here on a fresh enough 20-day break from a second two starts back.

runners_data.name: Head For Freedom
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby juveniles are always worth noting for course-and-distance fit, but this three-year-old's form has come over five and six furlongs rather than seven — stepping up in trip on 30 days off on good ground is a lot to ask despite the yard's recent 14-day strike rate.
runners_data.comment: Head For Freedom has shown enough encouragement — fourth three starts back and again fourth five starts back — to pose a serious threat here, and our rating of 71 ranks him second of 18 in the field; the risk is that he has been winless in his last five starts and must bounce back from an eighth last time out.

runners_data.name: Gwen's Girl
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's three-year-old returns after 93 days and has been running over eight to ten furlongs; dropping in trip to seven furlongs may be logical given her form but the lack of any win or place on good ground across her career is concerning.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Gwen's Girl has been consistently out of the frame in recent outings, and a 93-day break adds to the queries; experience over today's trip and going is the one genuine positive she brings.

runners_data.name: Secret Testimony
runners_data.note: Declan Carroll's three-year-old is yet to place at seven furlongs or on good ground across five attempts — PJ McDonald is a class booking but this horse's profile does not fit the race shape, the trip, or the surface well enough to feature prominently.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Secret Testimony has little obvious appeal here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 52 days between runs leaves him reasonably fresh, but that is slim ammunition.

runners_data.name: Travis
runners_data.note: Geoffrey Harker's consistent five-year-old has placed in four of five good-ground starts including a win, and his three consecutive third-place finishes at seven and eight furlongs on good ground show he stays involved; he races as a hold-up type but has enough tactical speed to press up if the pace is modest.
runners_data.comment: Travis has run over today's trip and going before and arrives here 26 days fresh, carrying 136 lb from stall 15 with a rating of 72 that marks him as the top-ranked runner in the field; the concern is that he was unplaced last time out.

runners_data.name: Hatamoto
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's progressive three-year-old is the sole confirmed front-runner in the race and has won three of his last five, all on good ground at around eight furlongs — stepping back to seven furlongs on the same going with David Allan aboard looks ideal, and unchallenged control of the pace is a significant weapon.
runners_data.comment: Hatamoto won last time out and was second two starts back, but slipped to sixth three starts back, giving a mixed recent profile; he has experience over today's trip and going, and 135 lb from stall three is the weight to factor against his current official mark of 64.

runners_data.name: Rousham
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's three-year-old won at seven furlongs on good ground and placed over six furlongs on the same surface — the form fits, and Alex Jary's 3lb claim is useful; 54 days off is a minor flag but the horse's natural hold-up style has genuine good-ground credentials here.
runners_data.comment: Rousham has run over today's trip and going, and a win four starts back shows he can get to the front, but a sixth last time out and a trainer without a winner in 22 recent attempts are harder to overlook at 134 lb from stall 14.

runners_data.name: Bleep Test
runners_data.note: Second string from Tim Easterby's powerful yard, this three-year-old has nine runs on good ground and has placed in four of those — the stable's focus appears to be on Hatamoto from the front, and Bleep Test's form figures in bigger fields on this surface are modest.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and held back by modest recent efforts, Bleep Test does bring distance and going experience to the table, and 32 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh, though her figures leave her with plenty to find against stronger company here.

runners_data.name: Sailor Batt
runners_data.note: David & Nicola Barron's three-year-old returns after 146 days off — that lengthy break is the dominant factor, and while placed efforts have come at seven and eight furlongs on softer surfaces, his good-ground record is sparse and the fitness question is genuine.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Sailor Batt does at least offer two thirds in recent outings as encouragement, and he has run over today's trip before, though 146 days off the track and a career-high 133 lb from stall 16 make this a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Black Rock Beauty
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's three-year-old won at seven furlongs on good ground and the form line has recent positive content — Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim helps, but as a hold-up type forced into a midfield slot in a slowly-run race with limited pace to close into, the natural game is constrained.
runners_data.comment: Black Rock Beauty has finished ninth last time out and sixth two starts back, leaving him hard to fancy from stall 10, and ranked 13 of 18 on our figures; a win four starts back offers a crumb of hope, and he does have experience of today's distance and going.

races.paceDynamic: Hatamoto is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to pressure him — he can dictate from the front at a comfortable, sustainable gallop on good ground over seven furlongs at Redcar. With the pace unchallenged, this race is set to be run at a rhythm that suits a prominent racer who can sit just off the leader and pounce, rather than a deep closer who needs a strong pace to close into. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types, but a significant number — including Camera Shy, Black Rock Beauty, Uncertainty and Mayo County — are true hold-up or prominent horses redistributed into midfield on the map because the field cannot accommodate all of them at the rear; those horses will not all get the gaps they need in a slowly-run race. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours Hatamoto himself and any runner capable of racing prominently and travelling smoothly into the race, with deep closers disadvantaged by a pace that is unlikely to be strong enough to set up a late swoop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hatamoto Leads & Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Hatamoto dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and kicks clear entering the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Hatamoto has a clean lead with no pressure, sets a pace that suits his own stamina profile, and is already hitting form having won three of his last five on good ground at this sort of trip; David Allan rides him confident knowing nothing will challenge early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Hatamoto weakens late and a horse travelling prominently just behind delivers a smooth challenge at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: With a steady gallop, horses racing just off the pace — Emery Down and Travis — will be travelling well within themselves and have enough gas left to overhaul a weakening leader in the final furlong; both have placed records on good ground at seven furlongs that make this shape credible.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Get Lucky
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses badly in the final quarter-mile and the field bunches, creating a brief but genuine late surge opportunity for hold-up types.
scenarios.body: This shape requires Hatamoto to stop sharply and the field to compress enough for horses like Luminous Warrior and Finn Ironside to arrive from off the pace — possible but dependent on an implosion that a strong Tim Easterby-trained leader is unlikely to provide.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If a wide, slow-run race results in no clear winner emerging from the front and the finish is a scrappy contest between several equally-positioned midfielders.
scenarios.body: With so many horses crammed into the midfield section due to redistribution, a chaotic finish with no clean run is possible; Rousham, who has won and placed on good ground over seven furlongs, and Black Rock Beauty, who brings a win at this trip on good ground, are best-placed to benefit from a messy conclusion.

watchPoints.text: Hatamoto (Tim Easterby/David Allan) has complete control of the pace — if he jumps cleanly and goes unchallenged to the front, he could prove very hard to peg back from the two-furlong pole given three wins on this surface.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Camera Shy, Black Rock Beauty, Uncertainty, Mayo County) will all be seeking positions that the race shape cannot provide — watch for traffic problems and blocked runs in the straight as 18 runners compact into limited space.

Travis has placed in four of five good-ground starts and could emerge as the stealthy danger if Hatamoto's pace is just slow enough to allow Oisin McSweeney to creep into contention — the three consecutive thirds show he finds a way to be involved.

Emery Down (Pat Cosgrave) is the prominent type most likely to sit closest to Hatamoto and is worth monitoring from the off — if he travels smoothly into the final two furlongs, his recent placed form at seven furlongs on good ground makes him a live player.

Cavallo Pazzo's 335-day layoff and Sailor Batt's 146-day absence mean both could need the run badly — watch their prices shorten or lengthen in the market as a guide to stable confidence before the off.

runners_data.name: Thunder Wonder
runners_data.note: Hold-up type stepping back to Good ground where he has a strong record (13/15 in similar conditions), but has been racing over shorter recently; Charlie Johnston in solid recent form and Callum Shepherd is a capable booking at this level.
runners_data.comment: Thunder Wonder has run over today's trip and going, and that third two starts back — plus a rating of 86 — marks him as a genuine danger here; the concern is that he remains winless in recent starts and a 39-day absence adds a fitness question.

runners_data.name: Golden Redemption
runners_data.note: Progressing handicapper whose last five runs were all over sprint distances — the step to 1m2f is a significant query; a genuine hold-up horse whose natural position at the rear is squeezed by the volume of closers in this field, which tempers confidence in his getting a clean run.

runners_data.name: Percy's Daydream
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for David O'Meara who has finished fourth in four of his last five starts on Good ground — handles this trip well and Kevin Stott keeps the ride, suggesting the yard expects another bold show if not quite a win.

runners_data.name: Lucky Hero
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted three-year-old for O'Meara who has won twice over 1m on Good ground recently; hold-up style suits a truly run race and Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim is a tangible asset, though jumping to 10f for the first time since a maiden is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Per Contra
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up performer for Tim Easterby who carries a headgear flag and has run only 10 days ago — the quick return on Good ground is fine for him, but his true off-the-pace style is constrained by how many closers populate this field, and his form figures on Good going (0W2P) are modest.
runners_data.comment: Per Contra returns in good time after finishing third last time out, and has run over today's trip and going before. Winless in his last six starts, though his speed rating of 88 makes him competitive carrying 135 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Farasi Lane
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran hold-up horse who has shown brief revival signs, winning at 8f on Good recently; the step up to 1m2f is an unknown quantity at his age, and his natural preference for coming late puts him in the same crowded category of closers who cannot all find clear racing room.
runners_data.comment: Farasi Lane showed his best when winning four starts back, but has managed only a third since in his last six, and his consistency is the concern here; he has experience over today's trip and going, and 134 lb from stall 3 gives him every chance to land a blow if recapturing that earlier form.

runners_data.name: Yafreh
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a pattern of placed efforts over 1m2f+ on Good ground (0W1P in similar conditions); a true hold-up racer whose finishing thrust is held back by the sheer number of horses seeking the same late ground — Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim is a mild plus.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Yafreh has little obvious appeal, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a return to placing form — he was second two starts back and second three starts back — offers a faint glimmer after 53 days off.

runners_data.name: Sea The Power
runners_data.note: Confirmed sole front-runner who shaped well to win on Soft going and steps onto Good ground for the first time over this trip; low-weighted at 127lbs and with Dale Swift holding the reins, his ability to control the tempo unchallenged is the defining factor in how this race is run.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Sea The Power has struggled for consistency in recent starts — a seventh, then a win, followed by sixth, ninth and fifth — and he is hard to fancy here, though he does have experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Lillie Margot
runners_data.note: Improving three-year-old prominent racer for Jedd O'Keeffe who won over 1m on Good ground and placed at shorter; stepping up in trip for the first time since a maiden win, James Sullivan keeps the partnership going and she handles the going well.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Lillie Margot is hard to fancy despite a win three starts back and a third two starts back; she has gone off the boil since, finishing fourth last time out, though experience on today's going and a 40-day break at least give her a fair chance to show something.

races.paceDynamic: Sea The Power is the sole confirmed front-runner and will set a controlled, uncontested pace on Good ground at Redcar over 1m2f — with no rival likely to pressure him early, the tempo will be honest but not punishing. Fox Avatar, Percy's Daydream and Lillie Margot will push to sit prominently just behind, creating a compact early order with genuine coverage across the first half of the race. This field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can place at the rear — Golden Redemption, Yafreh, Per Contra and Farasi Lane are all true hold-up horses shuffled into midfield on the map, meaning they will likely be bunched in the middle third rather than enjoying a clean run from off the pace. A controlled single-pace scenario on a flat track over a strong-staying trip favours prominent racers who can travel close to the tempo without burning fuel — horses tracking the leader from positions two to four are ideally placed to pounce as the pace naturally lifts over the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Sea The Power sets a steady solo gallop and horses tracking in second to fourth sweep past him entering the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: The moderate early fractions allow prominent types to conserve energy before quickening off the back of the pace; on Redcar's flat, undemanding straight, horses who travel fluently close to the leader rarely get run out of it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Sea The Power's uncontested lead becomes so comfortable that he steals enough margin to repel the challengers late.
scenarios.body: A lone front-runner on Good ground in a handicap over 1m2f can absolutely last home if the field behind fails to coordinate a pursuit early enough; Sea The Power's youth and low OR give him room to do this at a lenient mark.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply mid-race, stringing the field and creating genuine daylight for runners held off the pace to motor home.
scenarios.body: Despite being shuffled toward midfield on the map, Nepal and Lucky Hero are the most genuinely effective at coming from off a true pace; if the gallop suddenly lifts, their ability to produce a sustained late run gives them a meaningful chance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Sea The Power crawls and the entire field concertinas, turning the race into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A slow-run race over 1m2f on flat ground can favour those with a sharp turn of foot rather than true stayers; this benefits Thunder Wonder and Lillie Margot, both of whom have shown the ability to quicken from a compressed pace.

watchPoints.text: Sea The Power holds total control of the early pace — if he quickens his sectionals approaching halfway, the horses bunched in midfield may find themselves unable to reach the prominent racers in time.

Golden Redemption, Yafreh, Per Contra and Farasi Lane are all true hold-up horses compressed into midfield — watch for traffic trouble in the straight if they try to find gaps simultaneously from similar positions.
Lucky Hero steps up significantly in trip to 1m2f — watch his early demeanour and how he travels in the first half-mile, as any signs of pulling or greenness could compromise his late run.
Percy's Daydream has finished fourth in four of his last five starts — watch whether Kevin Stott opts for a more aggressive stalking position than usual to prevent another near-miss result.
Fox Avatar's recent form includes three runs on Standard ground where his figures dropped — watch early to confirm he is travelling as smoothly on Good turf as his best efforts suggest he can.

races.name: Constant Security Services Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Promethean
runners_data.note: Hold-up type dropping back to 12f from recent 16-17f efforts; 117 days off the track is a significant concern, and his poor recent form (0098-0) makes it hard to find a route into this race even if the pace suits late runners.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 117 days away, Promethean's recent form makes uncomfortable reading, but he has experience over today's distance and going, and a rating of 83 puts him narrowly top of these.

runners_data.name: Chesneys Charm
runners_data.note: Hector Crouch partners a mare who wants to race much closer to the speed than the map shows — her last five runs are all at 7-10f and she steps up sharply to 12f here, which is an untested trip; the furtado yard is in active form (T14: 1/23) but the distance query is real.
runners_data.comment: Chesneys Charm finished third last time out and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 76 putting him firmly in contention from stall nine on a workable 18-day break; the main concern is a trainer badly out of form at just 4% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Bay Dream Believer
runners_data.note: Three wins from nine on good ground is the standout going stat in this field and Jason Hart is an accomplished pilot, but she is a natural hold-up performer now squeezed into a midfield slot by the volume of similar runners — traffic is the genuine threat to her chances, not ability.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out but only fifth two starts back, Bay Dream Believer brings distance and going experience to this, and her 18-day turnaround looks sharp enough; the 137 lb burden from stall 10 may test her, however, against a competitive field at this level.

runners_data.name: Phantom Shadow
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter for this race and the key tactical fulcrum; the horse has placed at 10f on good ground and Ewan Whillans has placed him well recently (T14: 1/11), though as a natural prominent-racer rather than a true front-runner, Phantom Shadow's ability to sustain the lead for a full 1m2f is the central question.
runners_data.comment: Phantom Shadow has shown he can win, with a victory two starts back and a second three starts back, but a seventh last time out is concerning and our rating ranks him eighth of ten in this field. Has run over today's trip and going, but the burden of 135 lb makes appeal limited.

runners_data.name: Talitha Rouge
runners_data.note: Remarkable consistency on good ground — all five recent runs on good have produced a placing, including a second over this exact 12f trip; Mark Winn rides for the in-form David O'Meara operation (T14: 4/47) and the 25-day freshener looks ideal for a 3yo filly with proven stamina credentials.
runners_data.comment: Talitha Rouge arrives here fresh off a second last time out, and with a third three starts back, she has shown enough consistency to rank her as a leading danger despite being yet to score; the main risk is that sixth two starts back raises questions about her reliability.

runners_data.name: Kartini
runners_data.note: Steps back up from 8f to a more suitable 10f-plus distance and the Simon Whitaker yard has one runner qualified from five recently; her best effort was a second over 10f on standard, but two wins from eight on good ground is limited and she races at a weight (133lbs) that does not flatter.
runners_data.comment: Kartini arrives on the back of a second four starts back and holds experience over today's trip and going, with our rating of 74 suggesting she merits respect as a leading danger, though she remains winless in recent starts and consistency is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Woodleigh
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good ground nine days ago and Roger Fell runs horses back quickly when they are in form (T14: 3/16); as a true hold-up type displaced into a midfield slot, Oisin McSweeney will need to find a clear run in the straight — the short turnaround is worth noting for fitness rather than freshness.
runners_data.comment: Woodleigh won two starts back but was only sixth last time out, and while he has run over today's trip and going, that inconsistency is a concern; the 132 lb burden and a field ranking of seventh offer little encouragement despite his recent winning form.

runners_data.name: Port Darwin
runners_data.note: Two wins from nine on good ground at 9-10f and the Charlie Johnston yard is consistently active (T14: 2/32); naturally a hold-up horse now mapped centrally, but Callum Shepherd is an experienced claimer who can position pragmatically — the unexposed 3yo profile makes him one of the more interesting runners despite the style compromise.
runners_data.comment: Port Darwin won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and going in his favour, but a fourth last time out and 129 lb to carry give pause; lightly raced in this sphere, he sits in mid-division on ratings and will need a sharp return.

runners_data.name: Lightning Galaxy
runners_data.note: Form figures of 995948 tell a bleak story, and dropping back to 11-12f from shorter trips has not helped; the tongue-strap and cheekpiece headgear have not unlocked improvement, and ten placed finishes from fourteen on good with zero wins on that surface is a damning stat.
runners_data.comment: Lightning Galaxy has been winless in his last six starts, with an eighth last time out and little in the figures to inspire confidence ranked ninth of ten on our assessment; he has run over today's trip and going, and 13 days between runs at least means he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Forever Perfect
runners_data.note: Three consecutive good-ground runs have all come on Stanstead turf (artificial/standard) rather than genuine good, meaning her apparent sim-going profile is inflated; Kaiya Fraser is an apprentice claiming 5lbs but the 3yo filly's recent form (122300 fading to 0) does not suggest she is coming into this race in her best trim.
runners_data.comment: Three unplaced efforts in her last three starts make Forever Perfect hard to fancy, ranked bottom of this field on our figures, though she does bring going experience and a placed run two starts back offers a crumb of encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Phantom Shadow is the sole confirmed pace-setter and will lead from the front in what shapes up as a controlled, single-tempo affair over 1m2f on good ground at Redcar — a flat track that does not naturally suit front-runners but rewards those who can dictate an uncontested rhythm. With no genuine rival to press him early, Phantom Shadow's jockey P J McDonald will be able to set a measured gallop, meaning the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to string the field out and may actually compress the race into a single-file procession until the turn for home. This steady, unchallenged pace favours horses with a mid-to-late run in them who can respond to a quickening finish, particularly those with proven form over this trip in good ground conditions — Talitha Rouge and Bay Dream Believer fit that profile most closely. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear; Chesneys Charm, Bay Dream Believer, Port Darwin, Kartini, Woodleigh, Lightning Galaxy and Forever Perfect are all genuine come-from-behind horses, meaning several will be bunched in midfield competing for the same ground in the straight, which increases the chance of traffic issues and benefits those with cleaner positional options or a jockey able to find daylight early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Phantom Shadow Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Phantom Shadow is allowed to stride to the front unchallenged and controls the tempo throughout at a measured pace, negating any late challenge.
scenarios.body: Phantom Shadow sets a sustainable gallop that saps the finishing kick of the closers behind him, with PJ McDonald timing any acceleration from the 2f pole to stay ahead; the flat Redcar straight means a horse on the bridle turning in has a decisive positional advantage over those stuck in traffic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Thread Through
scenarios.trigger: If Phantom Shadow's gallop is just slow enough to leave the field bunched and one of the hold-up horses finds a clear passage at the right moment.
scenarios.body: The compressed midfield means a decisive late burst from a genuine stayer with a willing jockey can slice through tired rivals in the final furlong; Bay Dream Believer's three wins from fifteen on good ground and recent course form make her the most likely beneficiary, with Port Darwin's two wins at 9-10f on good also relevant.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Quickens Early
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up horses — most likely Port Darwin or Woodleigh — times a move earlier than normal and exploits a gap at the 3f marker before the sprint begins.
scenarios.body: Port Darwin's trainer Charlie Johnston excels at placing horses to strike fresh from handy positions and the horse's recent form string (615514) shows it knows how to win; Woodleigh won over 10f on good ground recently and Roger Fell's T14 ratio of 3/16 suggests the yard is in decent form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse — Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Phantom Shadow's early tempo proves entirely too slow and multiple runners simultaneously throw down their challenges in the straight, creating a scrappy blanket finish.
scenarios.body: A chaotic multi-horse sprint over the final furlong would randomise the outcome but would best suit a horse that can find a clear track without needing to switch — Talitha Rouge's consistent placing record (five placings from five recent Good-ground runs) suggests it rarely gets it wrong tactically; Promethean as a longer-priced outsider could also benefit from total confusion if given a straight run.

watchPoints.text: Bay Dream Believer's genuine hold-up style means Jason Hart must find a passage through a compressed midfield — if she meets a wall of horses at the 2f pole her chances evaporate regardless of ability.

Phantom Shadow's ability to sustain the lead for a full 10 furlongs is the race's defining question — if he weakens before the final furlong the entire scenario architecture shifts and the field will be caught flat.

Port Darwin is three years old and lightly raced, trained by Charlie Johnston who has form finding winning opportunities at this level — watch for an opening move from Callum Shepherd earlier than expected given the compressed field.

Woodleigh runs for the second time in nine days after a recent win; Roger Fell is happy to run horses back quickly but monitor paddock condition closely for any signs of the effort having taken its toll.

With seven horses genuinely wanting to close from behind, traffic incidents in the straight are more likely than usual — horses drawn to find a wide berth or with jockeys who commit earlier (Talitha Rouge, Port Darwin) are statistically better placed to avoid the scrimmage.

races.name: Constant Security Services Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Titian
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's eight-year-old veteran wears a hood and comes back quickly on 13 days' rest; recent form shows consistent sixth-to-fourth finishes over 9-10 furlongs on good ground, and while his sim-going record (1W1P from 8 runs) is modest, he at least handles the conditions reliably from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Titian arrives here in good order on a quick turnaround of 13 days, with experience of both today's trip and going in his favour, and a speed rating of 81 underlines his claims as the top-rated runner in this field; winless in his last five starts, he needs to convert.

runners_data.name: Golden Caviar
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's lightly-raced three-year-old has only three runs to his name and was placed on his penultimate outing on good ground; 33 days between runs and an unproven stamina profile at 1m2f are concerns, but the raw potential of a young horse with a Dunlop/Crouch combination warrants respect.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Golden Caviar faces a stiff task off 136 lb, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a third last time out offers a crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Al Fujairah
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner; Jack Callan can dictate every aspect of the race from gate to line, and three consecutive placed runs on good ground over shorter trips suggest progressive fitness, though stepping up to 1m2f for the first time is the key question mark.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and in solid nick, Al Fujairah has posted a second and a third in his last three starts and returns after 29 days in good order, with experience over today's trip and conditions in his favour; the chief risk is that he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Sutton Hoo
runners_data.note: Tagged as a fader who has not won or placed on good going in five attempts at similar conditions, and returning after 59 days off; the stamina flag and zero wins or places on good turf at this distance make this one hard to support in a race likely to be dominated by a front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Sutton Hoo advertises strong claims here: a winner three starts back and experience over today's trip and conditions, while his rating of 76 marks him out as a leading contender from stall one. The risk is two unplaced efforts since that victory.

runners_data.name: Sweet Kiss
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's mare has placed twice from nine starts on good ground at this sort of trip and arrives just 18 days after her last run in fine order; she is a genuine hold-up type by nature and, while shown in midfield here because so many closers contest this field, her chance hinges on Al Fujairah setting a pace that she can run into.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last six starts, Sweet Kiss does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and two seconds in that sequence show she can threaten; carrying 133 lb from stall three, the weight is the chief concern for a filly who finds winning hard to come by.

runners_data.name: Idyllic
runners_data.note: Wilf Storey's five-year-old has shown a placed run on soft over 10 furlongs but the sim-going record on good is unremarkable; a genuine hold-up runner by nature, here pushed into a midfield slot, and without a proven turn of foot over this trip on quick ground, his chance requires Al Fujairah to set a lung-busting gallop he is unlikely to face.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Idyllic has shown only occasional glimpses of form — a third two starts back her sole bright spot — and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, she faces a stiff task at 131 lb from stall eight, however she does have experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Lady Hornblower
runners_data.note: Jedd O'Keeffe's filly is the most natural prominent runner behind Al Fujairah and Jason Hart will ensure she slots into second; a variable form string (including a win) over shorter trips on good ground and her tendency to fade late (headgear: hood, stamina flag noted) make her a pace-dependent proposition.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Lady Hornblower nonetheless shaped with promise when third two runs back, has experience of today's distance and going, and a speed rating of 77 suggests she retains more ability than her mark of 62 implies; the risk is that her overall record in recent starts gives little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Man
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's three-year-old has a soft-ground bias across his recent form, has faded in his finishes, and carries a concern flag for fading; his natural hold-up style is squeezed into a midfield map position given the number of closers in this field, and the good ground at Redcar looks unlikely to showcase his best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with finishes including a ninth and eighth in that sequence, Cosmic Man is hard to fancy on these figures — ranked eighth of nine — though he has run over today's distance and going before and comes here fresh enough on 30 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Hey Havana
runners_data.note: Geoffrey Harker's three-year-old has placed in four of her last twelve starts and P J McDonald gives the partnership a boost; she is a genuine hold-up type represented in midfield on the map due to the crowded rear of the field, and her placed form over 7-11 furlongs suggests versatility, though she has never won.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a second three starts back, Hey Havana arrives on a quick 13-day turnaround with going experience to call on, but he remains winless in his last six starts and our rating of 66 suggests he faces a stiff task from stall 5 off 124 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Al Fujairah is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no rival likely to contest the lead on similar terms, will stride out unopposed from the gates over the straight Redcar mile-and-two on good ground. The absence of any genuine pace pressure means Al Fujairah can dictate a controlled, even tempo, conserving energy through the early stages and presenting a target that hold-up horses must reel in from a long way out. Several horses in this field — Sweet Kiss, Cosmic Man, Idyllic and Hey Havana — are genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed into midfield slots on the map because the field contains more rear-division runners than the race shape can absorb; Lady Hornblower is most likely to secure a prominent pitch behind Al Fujairah, with Titian and Golden Caviar tracking from midfield. A single, uncontested leader on a flat, galloping track in good conditions creates a race that strongly favours hold-up horses with a strong sustained finish, provided the pace is honest enough to stretch the field — but with only one setter, the danger is a falsely-run affair that plays instead into the hands of the closest tracker rather than those making late ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Al Fujairah Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Al Fujairah controls a measured but genuine pace and Lady Hornblower tracks in second without forcing the issue.
scenarios.body: Al Fujairah sets a sustainable tempo that depletes the closers' finishing reserves on the flat Redcar straight, leaving the confirmed hold-up horses with too much ground to recover when the winner kicks clear in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Get Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If Al Fujairah's pace is honest enough to string the field out and leave the backmarkers with a genuine target to aim at.
scenarios.body: Sweet Kiss and Titian, both showing recent place form at this trip on good ground, produce sustained finishes to swamp a tiring front-runner in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Al Fujairah crawls early and the field bunches, rewarding the horse closest to the pace at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Lady Hornblower, prominent throughout and suited by a sharp quickening contest over 1m2f, pounces as the gallop slows and hold-up horses cannot accelerate from too far back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Exploits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If midfield traffic or a muddling pace creates a scrambled finish in which a largely unexposed runner finds a clear run.
scenarios.body: Hey Havana, who has shown a habit of running into places and is ridden by P J McDonald, could benefit from a compressed finish where her decent recent form at the trip gives a subtle edge.

watchPoints.text: Al Fujairah's early sectionals — if Jack Callan is permitted to dawdle through the early stages unchallenged, the race could turn into a sprint finish that negates the closers entirely and hands Al Fujairah a straightforward win.

Sweet Kiss and Hey Havana are true hold-up horses mapped to midfield on the race shape; if the field bunches early behind a slow pace, both will be caught flat-footed with no clear run and their redistribution away from their natural position becomes a significant tactical handicap.

Lady Hornblower carries a stamina/fading flag over 1m2f — if Jason Hart commits to tracking Al Fujairah from an early stage, monitor whether she is still travelling at the two-furlong pole or beginning to weaken before the straight proper.

Sutton Hoo's 59-day absence combined with zero placed runs on good ground at this distance makes him a race-fitness watch; Conor Whiteley (5) on board means any greenness or sluggish reappearance could contribute to traffic problems for those tracking behind.

Golden Caviar is unproven beyond 10 furlongs and carries the uncertainty of a young three-year-old stepping into handicap company; Hector Crouch will need to position him carefully to ensure he is not caught wide or trapped behind slow runners if the pace compresses in the first half of the race.

races.name: Visit Racingtv.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Stormy Pearl
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with solid course form at 6f on good ground (12/15 sim-going, 1 win), trainer Thompson has 1 win from 9 in 14 days; ran 3rd here twice recently and will need to be produced late from the rear — compact pace is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Stormy Pearl has been remarkably consistent in recent starts, placed third three times in her last six, and at 18 days she arrives fresh enough to go again; she has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating has her sharing top billing, though she remains winless.

runners_data.name: Soul Warrior
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type with a fade-in-finish flag; only sim-going record shows 6 from 10 and form figures of 8-8-5 suggest more talent on paper than delivery — very wet/stamina tracks (STA) may have flattered it and good ground here needs respect.
runners_data.comment: Soul Warrior has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 58 ranks him third of seventeen, marking him as a genuine threat despite being winless in his last six starts — though a trainer currently without a winner in 22 attempts over the past fortnight is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Hurstwood
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up performer who won last time over this exact course, distance and going — 12/15 sim-going record is strong; at age 9 his form is quietly consistent and he represents a stable with modest recent numbers but the horse is in a good moment.
runners_data.comment: Hurstwood won last time out and returns in good order just 18 days later, bringing both distance and going experience to the table; at 135 lb from stall 17, the weight ask is the one factor to weigh against him.

runners_data.name: Blindfold Games
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who will be allowed to dictate on an uncontested lead; OR=55 for Edward Bethell who has a productive 14-day record (5/33), but the horse holds a style-fit flag of 0.93 as it is mapped as a prominent type — here it is genuinely leading, which is its best role and the flag is less relevant in this specific race shape.
runners_data.comment: Blindfold Games showed a glimpse of ability when second two starts back, yet has otherwise struggled in recent starts and remains yet to win, with 48 days off adding a fitness query; she has run over today's trip and carries 135 lb from stall three.

runners_data.name: Night Emperor
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a recent win over this course and distance on good ground (1 win from 8 sim-going runs); Warren Fentiman (3) claims 3lb and the combination of course form and a horse that handles this surface well makes it one of the more credible late-emerging dangers.
runners_data.comment: Night Emperor won two starts back and returns here fit on 18 days' rest, with experience of both today's trip and going conditions working in his favour; the main risk is that he has finished fourth or worse in four of his last six starts, suggesting consistency remains a concern.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Class
runners_data.note: 216 days off the track is a significant return concern; all recent starts came on standard (artificial) going at Southwell and the move to turf good is untested — 6/15 sim-going but those sim-going runs are not truly comparable, making this a hold-up type operating in uncertain conditions.
runners_data.comment: Sovereign Class is yet to win in her last five starts and returns after a 216-day absence, which is a significant query, though she does bring distance and going experience to the table and her speed rating offers mild encouragement from stall 14.

runners_data.name: Ridgemaster
runners_data.note: Consistent placer (2nd three times in last five) who is a genuine hold-up runner by nature but, with the field overloaded at the rear, has been pushed into a midfield mapping that does not reflect its true finishing style — the redistribution is real and its chances hinge on finding space it may not get.
runners_data.comment: Ridgemaster has been a model of consistency at the business end, placing second twice in his last two starts, though he remains yet to win in recent starts and that seventh three starts back is a blemish; experience over today's trip and going, plus a quick 14-day turnaround, keep him competitive from stall 2.

runners_data.name: Golden Prosperity
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing seven-year-old who handles good ground well (13/15 sim-going, 1 win, 5 places) and has the profile to track Blindfold Games from a handy position; Conor Whiteley claims 5lb and the horse's course form over 6f on good ground is the best placed record in the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Golden Prosperity does offer some encouragement — a second two starts back and two thirds in recent form suggest ability, though the seventh last time out is less inspiring; has run over today's trip and going, and arrives on a sharp 14-day turnaround carrying 129 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Brave Bob
runners_data.note: True hold-up type by nature, shunted into midfield on the map because of redistribution pressure — all five recent runs came on standard going at Southwell or Flat turf, and the step up to good turf is a genuine unknown; Julie Camacho sends it out after 65 days off with a style-fit flag that should temper expectations.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Brave Bob has shown some promise with a second and third in recent outings, but a 65-day absence and a stiff 129 lb from stall 15 are the hurdles he faces, and his official rating of 47 leaves him with plenty to find against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Ziva's Star
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up runner whose best recent finish was 2nd over this course and distance on good going — the redistribution forward is purely a map necessity, not a reflection of its actual race plan; Andrew Elliott rides and headgear (blinkers) is noted, with 10/15 sim-going runs suggesting solid going suitability.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out but winless in her last six starts overall, Ziva's Star has experience of today's trip and going to call on, though an official rating of 46 and draw ten at 128 lb leave her needing to find improvement to get competitive here.

runners_data.name: Pinpoint
runners_data.note: Placed three times on good going over 5-6f and showed a 2nd last time over 6f on good (sim-going: 8/15, 1 win, 3 places) — a hold-up runner pushed to midfield on the map, but its closing ability is genuine; fresh off 32 days, the fitness question is mild but the form profile is quietly solid.
runners_data.comment: Pinpoint arrives third last time out and placed second three starts back, though winless in his last five; he has experience over today's distance and going, and 32 days between runs leaves him reasonably fresh, but a mark of 46 and stall 13 underline the task from mid-field.

runners_data.name: Long Shot
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Tim Easterby who has a strong 14-day strike-rate (14/81) and David Allan takes the ride — natural finisher who has placed three times on good ground but, displaced to midfield by redistribution, cannot guarantee the position it needs; 2nd last time over 6f on good is a positive data point.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Long Shot nevertheless shows a degree of consistency with three fourth-place finishes and a second in recent form; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 21 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, though 127 lb from stall one may test his resolve.

runners_data.name: Ninety Nine
runners_data.note: 96 days off the track is a red flag for a horse whose recent form figures read 07-070 — placed just once in five recent starts and all five came over 5f, making the step to 6f a concern; Jason Hart rides but the redistribution from hold-up to midfield compounds an already difficult profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked well down the field on our figures, Ninety Nine is hard to fancy here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns after 96 days carrying 127 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Captain Bentley
runners_data.note: Fade-in-finish flag accompanies a hold-up style for this seven-year-old; form of 000-68 over 5-6f on good/soft tells a story of a horse that struggles to land a blow, and the redistribution forward does not change the underlying evidence — James Sullivan rides but the profile is one of the weakest in the race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Captain Bentley has been out of the frame in three consecutive outings prior to a sixth two starts back and an eighth last time out, making him very hard to fancy despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Hyrcanian
runners_data.note: Three fade-in-finish flags and a recent run of 14th on good going over 6f — Ron Barr's runner has a blank 14-day record and returns after 70 days; a hold-up type that has rarely competed at this level effectively and the redistribution to midfield is an optimistic placement it is unlikely to justify.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Hyrcanian faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's distance and going before, and 127 lb from stall 12 are the bare facts to weigh after a 70-day absence.

runners_data.name: Lesley Buckley
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly with a fade flag and hold-up style, last seen 3rd over 5f on good (sim-going only 3/9); Pat Cosgrave's experience is an asset but the horse has largely disappointed over 6-7f on turf tracks and the short sim-going sample on comparable conditions offers little confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 14th of 17 on our figures, Lesley Buckley faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and a third three starts back shows she can hit the frame on her day.

runners_data.name: Breeze Star
runners_data.note: Fade-in-finish flag and a form string of 8-8-7-8-9 across five starts on good and soft — Linda Perratt's juvenile has not threatened yet and the redistribution to midfield is a mapping necessity rather than a tactical advantage; with a style-fit flag of 0.92 and no win or place form to speak of, this is among the least likely winners.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with finishes no better than seventh in recent starts, Breeze Star rates well below the field on our figures and is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick enough turnaround at 16 days.

races.paceDynamic: Blindfold Games is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a 17-runner field on good ground over 6f at Redcar, is likely to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested tempo rather than a scorching one. That controlled early pace means the race will be run at an honest but not brutal gallop, with the peloton likely to race in a fairly compressed group behind, reducing the premium on raw closing ability. The race shape marginally favours horses who can travel prominently or in the first half of the field and produce a sustained effort through the final two furlongs, rather than true hold-up horses who need a strong pace to reel back. Critically, the field holds far more genuine hold-up types than can realistically be accommodated at the rear — Ridgemaster, Long Shot, Brave Bob, Pinpoint, Ziva's Star, Ninety Nine and others are mapped to midfield precisely because they have been displaced forward by the congestion of hold-up runners, and their redistribution should be viewed with scepticism; the horses most likely to actually secure a forward position are Golden Prosperity and Blindfold Games, with Stormy Pearl, Hurstwood and Night Emperor likely tracking in mid-division.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Blindfold Games Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Blindfold Games sets a steady, uncontested pace and the field fails to reel it back through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Blindfold Games dictates its own fractions on the front end with no rival willing or able to match it early, conserving enough energy to hold on; prominent-tracking runners like Golden Prosperity and Night Emperor are best placed to pounce if it ties up, but may simply not get close enough.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Delivery Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough that a prominent or mid-division tracker can sustain a run from two furlongs out to collar the leader close home.
scenarios.body: A runner travelling well just off the pace — within three lengths of Blindfold Games — produces the most efficient finish by converting early positioning into a sustained effort rather than a late burst; Golden Prosperity and Night Emperor have the profiles to do exactly this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Hold-Up Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace ends up sharper than expected and genuinely redistributed hold-up horses find themselves in a better position than the map suggests.
scenarios.body: Ridgemaster and Long Shot have solid placed form in similar conditions and could benefit if the field fans wide on the home turn, creating a clear passage; both are genuine hold-up types who need every yard of the 6f to produce their effort and are reliant on the pace raising the tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Big Field Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the large 17-runner field causes significant early crowding, position changes and interrupted rhythms that neutralise pace advantages entirely.
scenarios.body: Fractured early running disrupts Blindfold Games' ability to lead cleanly and compresses the field into a pack finish where small advantages in draw or luck in running become decisive; horses on the outside with clean air — such as Brave Bob and Pinpoint — could steal a march but both carry style-fit caveats.

watchPoints.text: Blindfold Games is the sole front-runner in a 17-runner field — watch if P J McDonald presses the advantage early and opens a gap, as any slow reaction from the chasing pack could let it steal an unassailable lead.

Golden Prosperity is the most naturally prominent horse behind the leader and if it secures a position on Blindfold Games' quarters, it becomes the primary danger throughout — watch its early positioning as a direct threat indicator.

Night Emperor's recent course-and-distance win on good ground makes it a legitimate tracking threat, but Warren Fentiman (3) on a 17-runner flat handicap creates potential for positional errors — watch the first furlong to see if the claim rider gets a clean passage.

With seven or more horses tagged as redistributed hold-up types all needing late runs in a potentially steady-paced race, watch for a wall of horses arriving late but finding the leader too far gone — the finishing straight could be congested without a decisive winner emerging from the pack.

Ridgemaster's three placed efforts in its last five starts on good-ish going make it a quiet danger if it finds a clear run, but watch whether its true hold-up style is fatally compromised by starting further forward than it prefers in such a large field.
