runners_data.name: Lever Up
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who has struggled in similar conditions (no wins from 9 runs on Good-equivalent going); the 57-day break is a query, and without a strong pace to close into, his chance is structurally limited here.
runners_data.comment: Rated highest of the 20 runners here, Lever Up showed real promise when third two starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions; the concern is 57 days off the track and a winless recent run of form.

runners_data.name: Degale
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator whose record on Good ground reads 11 runs, 1 win, 5 places but all at 8f — this mile trip and a field without a proper pace reduces his chance of getting competitive late; trainer Barron is 0/11 over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of twenty by our rating and carrying a useful speed figure of 78, Degale has run over today's distance and going before and arrives here on a fitness-friendly 26-day break — though he remains winless in his last six starts, with only a third two runs back to show from recent efforts.

runners_data.name: Yafaarr
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with genuine claims — won on Good ground over 8f and placed twice more on similar ground, stepping back to a mile he has won over; trainer Sam England is in form (3/21 over 14 days) and this represents a live contender racing in his natural position.

runners_data.name: We've Got This
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has placed at this trip on Good ground, but the 48-day absence and tendency to find only a handful of rivals in front make this a speculative entry; Elle-May Croot's 5lb claim helps offset the weight.
runners_data.comment: Placed two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, We've Got This rates well above her official mark and lines up from stall 3 carrying 137 lb, but 48 days off the track and a trainer firing at just 4% make confidence hard to hold.

runners_data.name: Perfidia
runners_data.note: Extremely strong profile for this shape — 13 runs on Good ground producing 2 wins and 9 places, races prominently, and her recent form includes two second-place finishes; David Allan's experience in big-field handicaps at this level is a significant plus.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a winner five starts back, Perfidia has experience over today's trip and going to call upon, but a seventh two starts back tempers enthusiasm; carrying 137 lb from stall 13, he shapes as a honest mid-division type at best.

runners_data.name: Pisanello
runners_data.note: The most compelling hold-up horse in the field — three wins from his last five runs on Good ground, all at trips of 8-10f, and his tactical adaptability means he is likely to be closer to the action than a true backmarker; headgear (visor) applied, suggesting trainer David O'Meara expects a sharp effort.
runners_data.comment: Pisanello won three of his last six starts, with a runner-up finish last time out, and has experience of today's distance and going — positives that underpin a competitive profile. Carrying 137 lb from stall six after 31 days off gives the assessor pause, though his rating of 66 suggests residual ability.

runners_data.name: Havana Mojito
runners_data.note: Front-running/prominent type whose entire recent form is built on placing — six places from 13 on Good ground, but notably no wins since coming good; races close to the pace which suits this shape perfectly even if finding the winner elusive.
runners_data.comment: Havana Mojito has been a model of consistency in placing, with four seconds in his last six starts, yet he remains winless and that elusive breakthrough continues to evade him; a sixth last time out clouds matters, though he has distance and going experience to call on from stall five.

runners_data.name: The New Bay Pearl
runners_data.note: A hold-up type placed in the mid-division due to overcrowding at the rear — has shown consistent placing in Good-ground miles (four top-4 finishes from 14 runs) but no wins; racing out of his ideal position reduces his threat and the STYLE_FIT flag is a legitimate concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a string of fourths and a recent third doing little to inspire confidence, The New Bay Pearl ranks among the outsiders on these figures; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 28 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Yoko
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who is effectively racing out of role in a slow-pace scenario — only 10 days since last run, and a 3-year-old stepping up from 6-7f; the redistribution means he is unlikely to produce a true closer's finish from where the race places him.
runners_data.comment: Yoko has been winless in her last five starts, with a ninth two runs back among a string of mid-pack efforts, and she carries a stiff 129 lb from stall 16 — while she has run over today's trip and going and returns on a fresh ten days, a trainer without a winner in twenty attempts over the past fortnight makes her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Fate's Gambit
runners_data.note: True closer whose Good-ground record is sparse (2 from 9) and who faces the difficulty of being mapped forward of his natural position; 21 days since last run is acceptable, but the structural disadvantage of a single-pace race is hard to overcome.
runners_data.comment: Fate's Gambit arrives here 21 days fresh, has run over today's trip, and catches the eye with a third two starts back alongside a fourth last time out — yet to win in recent starts, and a trainer in lean form (1/28 over 14 days) is the one reservation carrying 129 lb from stall one.

runners_data.name: Balmoral Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up 3-year-old whose best effort was a second over 10f on Good ground — the step back to a mile with a single front-runner and a crowded mid-section means he is unlikely to replicate that effort from a displaced position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 19 of 20 on our figures, Balmoral Boy is hard to fancy, and a trainer without a winner in 22 attempts over the past fortnight compounds the concern; experience over today's trip and going, plus a return after just 15 days, are slim consolations.

runners_data.name: Oilisa
runners_data.note: 102-day absence is a significant flag, and while she won over this trip on Heavier ground, her Good-ground record (4 runs, 0 wins, 0 places) is uninspiring; mapped mid-division rather than her natural rear position, further complicating her chance.
runners_data.comment: Oilisa won five starts back, though two unplaced efforts since temper expectations, and 102 days off the track is a fitness query; she has run over today's trip and going, and carries 127 lb from stall 20.

runners_data.name: Here Comes Louie
runners_data.note: Only 7 days since last run and form includes two second-place finishes at 8f, but all on Tapeta/Standard rather than Good turf — the going switch and racing out of his preferred hold-up role are both concerns.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked last of the 20 runners on our figures, Here Comes Louie faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's trip and going before and was third last time out, with two seconds in recent starts offering slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Beckon
runners_data.note: Prominent type whose only win came on Standard going; form on Good and Soft has been poor (9th, 9th, 6th), but his racing style keeps him in contention if the pace is slow enough to play into his hands.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive ninth-place finishes make Beckon hard to fancy on recent form, and she is ranked near the foot of the field on our figures; she has run over today's trip and is at least fit enough on a 21-day break, but that is limited encouragement.

runners_data.name: Falcon Nine
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse who has been placed six times from 15 on Good ground and has two wins at this distance — likely to be positioned closer than his natural style given the redistribution squeeze; Jason Hart is a strong booking in big fields.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts despite three runner-up finishes, Falcon Nine is frustratingly consistent without converting, though his second two starts back suggests fair ability; he has run over today's distance and going before, and 16 days between runs leaves him reasonably fresh from stall eight carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Eeetee
runners_data.note: True hold-up veteran whose Good-ground record shows nine runs for 1 win and 2 places — the pace of this race is likely too moderate to generate the closing ground he needs, and form figures of 780-89 suggest he is out of form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Eeetee at least has experience over today's trip and conditions to call upon, though a string of mid-to-rear finishes makes improvement essential; 44 days off and a low draw from stall two are the variables to watch.

runners_data.name: Rwenearlytheredad
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner drawn to lead throughout, but a poor recent record (no wins, two places from 15 on Good) and 93-day absence temper confidence in him lasting once the prominent pack bears down in the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 93 days off, Rwenearlytheredad has experience of today's distance and going, and a rating edge over his official mark offers some encouragement, though his recent string of mid-pack finishes makes improvement hard to predict.

runners_data.name: Sunny Orange
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's strong form (14/81 over 14 days) and an excellent place record on Good ground (14/15) are notable, but this is a genuine hold-up horse who is pushed forward in the mapping; the 10-day turnaround is fine, but the race shape is structurally unkind to him.
runners_data.comment: Sunny Orange has shown consistent placing ability in recent starts — third and second figures pepper his record — but he remains yet to win in his last six outings, and a fourth last time out suggests he may again find one or two too good from stall nine carrying 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Captain Corelli
runners_data.note: A 9-year-old returning after 293 days — that absence alone makes him difficult to recommend, and while he carries significant Good-ground experience (11 runs), he has been in decline and races out of his natural position; the STYLE_FIT flag compounds this.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and not seen on a track for 293 days, Captain Corelli faces a stiff ask returning from such a lengthy absence, and his recent string of unplaced efforts offers little encouragement; he has run over today's trip and going, which is at least something to cling to.

runners_data.name: Leelawadee
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old hold-up type whose best effort was a second over 8f on Good ground; only 3 runs at this distance and a tendency to race prominently in her natural rhythm may help slightly, but trainer Dods' 14-day figures (2/30) are modest.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Leelawadee does bring distance and going experience to the table, and that second two starts back offers a flicker of encouragement, though she was seventh last time out and a rating of 60 ranks her well down the field.

races.paceDynamic: Rwenearlytheredad is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 20-strong field and, ridden by PJ McDonald, is expected to set a controlled, unhurried gallop on Good ground at Redcar over a mile — a track that rewards horses who travel prominently and don't get buried in traffic. With no genuine challenger for the lead, the pace is likely to be modest early before quickening in the home straight, which classically plays into the hands of prominent racers who can track close to the gallop and pounce as the tempo builds. Prominent types such as Yafaarr, Perfidia, Havana Mojito, We've Got This, and Beckon are best placed to exploit this setup, tracking the single pace-setter without burning energy. This race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-handy profile — horses racing just off a single sustainable lead, able to kick with the winner through the final two furlongs, rather than deep closers who need a true searching gallop to reel in the field. The field contains a significant overload of hold-up types — Sunny Orange, Yoko, Fate's Gambit, Balmoral Boy, Captain Corelli, Here Comes Louie, Oilisa, and The New Bay Pearl are all genuine closers who cannot all race from their natural position in a 20-runner field, and with only one pace-setter, the most likely to secure a useful position from behind are Falcon Nine and Pisanello, who have the tactical versatility and recent winning form to adapt.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Rwenearlytheredad sets a steady, uncontested pace and the race is decided by prominent horses kicking off the bend.
scenarios.body: Rwenearlytheredad dictates a moderate tempo, allowing Yafaarr, Perfidia, and Havana Mojito to travel smoothly just off the pace before unleashing their finish in the closing stages; Perfidia's strong record on Good ground (13/15) and Yafaarr's recent form make them ideal beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pisanello Stalks, Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace remains honest enough for Pisanello to travel smoothly in mid-division and produce his now trademark late burst.
scenarios.body: Pisanello arrives on the back of three wins in his last five starts on Good ground, and his ability to switch off behind the pace before delivering a sustained run makes him well suited to a race where hold-up horses are squeezed into mid-division, placing him closer than usual.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Runner Lasts
scenarios.trigger: If Rwenearlytheredad is given an absurdly easy lead and PJ McDonald slows the race to a crawl, stealing it with a perfectly timed sprint.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to pressure Rwenearlytheredad at any point, he could conserve enough energy to hold on through the final furlong as the pack makes up ground belatedly; this scenario demands everything to go perfectly for the leader and the prominent horses to be caught flat-footed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Closers Reel In
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes early scrimmaging that forces the pace higher and produces a truly run race where genuine hold-up horses can close.
scenarios.body: With 20 runners, erratic early positioning could push the tempo up and create room for a late-closing run, but this is structurally unlikely given only one front-runner and the redistribution of most closers into mid-division; Sunny Orange's strong place record on Good ground and Fate's Gambit offer the best prospects if conditions turn against the prominent runners.

watchPoints.text: Rwenearlytheredad's early pace dictates the entire shape — if PJ McDonald crawls in front and the field fails to chase, the race becomes a sprint and prominent types Perfidia and Yafaarr must be sharp off the bend to avoid being caught flat.

With 20 runners on a flat mile, early positional scrimmaging could push tempo higher than expected — watch for Havana Mojito and We've Got This being shuffled back further than their natural prominent position, which would help Pisanello if he slides forward.

Pisanello's visor application signals David O'Meara expects a more switched-on performance — if he travels smoothly in the first half-mile rather than dropping towards his usual rear position, he becomes the most dangerous horse in the race.

Sunny Orange and Fate's Gambit are mapped mid-field but are true hold-up horses — if either drifts back to their natural position during the race, they are racing in a shape that doesn't suit them and can be safely discounted late on.

Trainer Tim Easterby is firing (14/81 over 14 days) with both Perfidia and Sunny Orange in this race — Perfidia's prominent style is the one that aligns with the pace map, making her the more interesting of the two stable runners given this race shape.
